history.content: My AWS bill jumped from $90 to $400 this month. Figure out why.

Found it. AWS's own alert says the estimate is $402.11, and the jump is almost all EC2: $310, driven by data transfer out of us east 1. That pattern usually means something's shipping a lot of traffic out of AWS (large downloads, media serving, or a backup/sync job gone loud) rather than a compute spike. The alert email doesn't say which instance or how many GB, so the exact culprit is in the full billing console. Want me to pull up the AWS billing console to pinpoint the instance and the transfer volume?
